reason: The Competition Period (cl. 1C) runs from the deed until 2 years after it ends, and bars the business anywhere within 3 km except the Property. The 2 post-term years are a post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold, and are void. (The in-term part would on its own be a refer.)
A rent due date (cl. 1B) with interest on late payment. A time for payment that limits no claim and no recourse to court. (The interest itself raises nothing under ss.27-28.)
For 3 years after the lease, no rice and food trading from the same street or within 500 m. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void.
The invoice is payable if not objected to within 30 days, but the Lessee expressly keeps the right to dispute it later under the dispute resolution clause. No right is lost.
A written agreement to refer a difference that 'has arisen' (electricity charges for the past period) to arbitration by a jointly named chartered accountant. Saved by Exception 2.
A suit for the deposit is not maintainable unless instituted within 6 months of vacating, against 3 years (Arts. 55/113). Shortens the time to sue. Void.

Every invoice is 'deemed accepted ... in all respects' unless disputed within the Review Period (14 days, cl. 1C). A deemed-acceptance clause that takes away the right to dispute on the expiry of a period. Void.

No claim about lifts, air-conditioning or common services 'shall be entertained by any court, tribunal or arbitrator', and the Lessee agrees not to bring one. An absolute bar for that class of claims, overriding cl. 39. Void to that extent.

The Lessee agrees not to bring the Fit-out Claims (cl. I(f)) 'before any court or arbitral tribunal' and releases them. These are future claims about handover, so this is not a settlement of existing ones; it is an absolute bar for that class of claims. Void to that extent.
User clause: no canteen or restaurant, only an employee pantry. Restricts use of these premises only.
An indemnity, and the Lessor's liability is capped at its insurance recovery. Limits recovery, not access to court.

A claim not referred within 6 months after the lease ends is 'deemed to have been waived', and the other party 'shall stand discharged'. Waiver and discharge on the expiry of a period, against the 3-year period (s.43 of the 1996 Act). Void.
A claim for abatement is 'deemed to have been waived' unless made within 7 days of the event. The right is extinguished on the expiry of a period. Void.

An independent licensed surveyor appointed jointly, whose certificate on area is final and binding. An agreed way of fixing a fact; courts are not expressly excluded, and cl. 18(d) arbitration remains. Refer, per the BP-7 approach.
User clause: corporate office only, not a showroom, warehouse or guest house. Restricts use of these premises only.
A late fee of Rs. 500 a day on top of 12% interest. Whether the fee is a penalty is a s.74 question.

The lock-in sentence is unobjectionable. The second sentence bars software consulting from any competitor's building in Hyderabad for 3 years after the deed ends. A post-lease restraint; the rent concessions are not goodwill. Void to that extent.

The guarantee extinguishes the Lessors' rights, and discharges the bank, unless a claim is made within one year of the guarantee's expiry. A term in a bank guarantee with a period of not less than one year from a specified event, so it is saved by Exception 3.

The Damage Assessment is the Lessors' own (cl. A(v)), and it 'shall not be open to challenge ... before any court, arbitral tribunal or other authority'. One party decides and every forum is shut out. Void to that extent; the 15-day payment term alone would be fine.

The Lessor's action for repair costs is 'barred' after the Recovery Deadline (6 months after vacating, cl. 1D), against 3 years under Art. 55. Shortens the time to sue. Section 28 protects the Lessor too. Void.
A claim is 'barred' unless notice invoking arbitration is served within 3 months of the cause of action. Shortens the 3-year period, which applies to arbitration through s.43 of the 1996 Act. Void.

For one year after vacating, the Lessee must procure that its directors and key managers do not promote or hold an interest in any software business in Bangalore. A post-lease restraint (s.27 covers 'any one' restrained), with no goodwill sold. Void.
Lock-in: six months' rent as 'pre-estimated damages' on early termination. Whether that is a penalty is a s.74 question.
Obtain the licences within 60 days. An ordinary step under the contract.

The Lessor's own decision on maintenance charges is final and 'shall not be called in question ... in any court, before any arbitrator or ... any other authority'. One party decides and every forum is shut out, overriding Article 20. Void to that extent.
The Jurisdiction City is Bangalore, where the premises are (cl. 1C). Those courts have jurisdiction anyway (Hakam Singh, A.B.C. Laminart), and cl. 26 arbitration stands alongside.

Noida courts only, and the premises are in Noida. Those courts have jurisdiction over the property anyway. (It conflicts with cl. 14.6.4, which names Delhi, but it does not shut out a competent court.)
Delay-compensation claims go to arbitration under the 1996 Act ('shall be referred'). A binding arbitration agreement for that class of claims. Saved by Exception 1.

The Limitation Date (cl. I(g)) is 3 years from the cause of action, the same as the Limitation Act period for money claims under a lease (Arts. 52, 55, 113). Not shorter, so not void. (If it were read to reach the Lessor's suit for possession, which has 12 years under Art. 67, it would be void to that extent; I do not read 'claim under this Deed' that way.)

'Notwithstanding clause 14.6.3', the Lessor's own decision on area is final and may not go to arbitration or be questioned in any court. One party decides and every forum is shut out. Void to that extent.
Damages are to be an adequate remedy for parking, and the right to an injunction is waived. The court stays open for damages, so this is a remedies question, not s.28.

In-term only, but it bars the Lessee from occupying any other premises within 2 km for its business. That is business elsewhere, not use of these premises, and the landlord's interest is not apparent (as PO-11, PO-39). Refer.

The gymnasium goodwill is sold to the Lessee, but the Lessor's restraint runs for a fixed 10 years 'irrespective of whether the Lessee continues to run the gymnasium', and statewide. Exception 1 requires the restraint to last only so long as the buyer carries on a like business. Void.

A renewal option exercisable by notice 6 months before expiry, and it lapses if not exercised. A time limit on exercising an option is part of the option itself; it does not restrict enforcement of an accrued right. Valid.

Two years after leaving, no financial information services from competing technology parks in Noida. A post-lease restraint; the recital of the Lessor's 'legitimate interest' does not help, since s.27 has no reasonableness test outside Exception 1. Void.
Forfeiture of advance rent if possession is not taken within 60 days. A s.74 question.
For six months after the lease, no medical transcription office within 1 km. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void however short.

The Lessee is 'deemed to have waived' its refund of the deposit, and the Lessor 'shall stand discharged', unless a written claim is lodged within 60 days of handover. Waiver and discharge on the expiry of a period. Void.
The Lessor will not allow a competitor's signage on the facade during the term. A restriction on how the Lessor deals with its own property, in-term only.

On its own this is void: arbitration only 'if both parties so agree at the time' is not an arbitration agreement (Jagdish Chander), and suits are barred, so it is an absolute bar. But cl. 23A of this deed sends 'any question, difference or dispute' to arbitration with 'shall', so a forum is left if 23A governs. The two need reading together (as PO-59). Refer; worth discussing.

'Designated Courts' are the courts at Chennai (cl. I(h)), but nothing in the deed connects Chennai to this lease. The premises and the Lessor are in Coimbatore, the Lessee's registered office is in Bangalore, and the deed was executed at Coimbatore. Parties cannot confer jurisdiction on a court that has none (A.B.C. Laminart). An 'exclusive' submission to such a court ousts the competent courts and leaves none, so it is void. Article XXIX (Coimbatore) also points the other way. Only if some part of the cause of action arose in Chennai would this become a refer.
Deliver the Insurance Certificate (cl. 1D) within 30 days of renewal. An ordinary step under the contract.

The Lessor will not let space to a BPO company during the Protected Period (cl. 1D), which is the lease period plus 2 years. During the term it is valid (a restriction on the Lessor's own property); the post-term 2 years are the doubtful part (as PO-43). Refer.
The Lessor's own surveyor measures, and the Lessee 'cannot challenge it in court or in arbitration'. A party's nominee plus an express exclusion of every forum (as PO-49). Void.

The cafeteria business and its goodwill are sold to the Lessee, and the restraint lasts while the buyer carries on a like business, but it runs 'anywhere in India'. That is not a specified local limit, so Exception 1 does not apply (as PO-68). Void.
